text:
TREC Product Recommendation 2025 provides a useful annotation taxonomy: functional substitutes, conceptual substitutes, complements with supported/unknown/incompatible compatibility, unrelated items, and unable-to-assess. Its coarse substitute definition explicitly allows different photographic purposes, so functional relatedness alone cannot establish a specific-purpose match. For this task, add separate purpose-fit and duplicate-identity labels, requiring explicit title/description evidence; shared words or similar titles establish neither compatibility nor identical products. This is a proposed adaptation of the [TREC rubric](https://trec-product-search.github.io/recommendations.html), not an established diagnostic result.

Uncertainty needs explicit evaluation. [AbstentionBench (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09038) finds that stronger reasoning does not reliably solve abstention. [Can LLM be a Personalized Judge? (2024)](https://aclanthology.org/2024.findings-emnlp.592/) reports low overall agreement with human preferences, with better agreement on high-certainty cases. Accordingly, require evidence spans and permit unknown for purpose, identity, and compatibility independently. Histories and timestamps provide behavioral context, not proof of current needs, ownership, or diversity/conformity traits.

Proposed validation: independently annotate the twenty training users’ feedback against these definitions, retaining ambiguous cases and adjudicating disagreements. Measure per-label precision/recall where feedback explicitly supports a judgment, annotation agreement, abstention coverage, and error rate among assessed cases; report counts by category and user. Missing feedback is unassessed, not a negative label. Separate rubric development from assessment, preferably using held-out users or leave-one-user-out checks, and acknowledge the small sample. These diagnostics remain exploratory proxies; model selection continues to use the pinned macro validation HR@10.
